## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Lokuttarakusala* ("Supramundane Wholesome", Ds 2.1.5) is a major analytical section within the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the first book of the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. In the systematic architecture of the text, following the initial tripartite division of dhammas outlined in the *mātikā*, wholesome phenomena (*kusala-dhammas*) are examined across different spheres of existence: the sense sphere (*kāmâvacara*), fine-material sphere (*rūpâvacara*), immaterial sphere (*arūpâvacara*), and the supramundane (*lokuttara*) [Gethin 2001]. In secondary reference literature and later manuals, the term *lokuttarakusala* is predominantly discussed doctrinally as the four transcendent path-consciousnesses (*magga-citta*) that directly eradicate defilements.

SuttaCentral does not record any curated parallels for Ds 2.1.5, though it lists two modern translations in two languages [SuttaCentral]. Computationally, DharmaNexus detects extensive Pali-internal text reuse (10,259 matching passages across 97 texts), reflecting the highly formulaic structure of Abhidhamma psychological matrices [DharmaNexus]. Its highest internal reuse occurs with other analytical sections of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, notably *Kāmāvacarakusala* (Ds 2.1.1), *Lokuttaravipāka-paṭhamamaggavipāka* (Ds 2.1.8), *Rūpāvacarakusala* (Ds 2.1.2), *Dvādasa akusala* (Ds 2.1.6), and *Abyākatavipāka* (Ds 2.1.7) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, extensive shared phrasing connects this section with analytical treatises in the *Vibhaṅga*, such as the *Saccavibhaṅga* (Vb 4), *Maggaṅgavibhaṅga* (Vb 11), *Iddhipādavibhaṅga* (Vb 9), and *Satipaṭṭhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 7) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-linguistically, DharmaNexus identifies algorithmic alignments with various Sanskrit and Tibetan scholastic works treating doctrinal lists, including the *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, the *Mahāvyutpatti*, and Śāntideva's *Śikṣāsamuccaya* [DharmaNexus].
